structure.scope: A1, A2, B1 and B2 — every level, each read from an official candidate paper. B1 also carries a post-2024 figure from the reform notice, because the reform changed B1 and only B1.

sources.what: DELF A1 tout public, official candidate paper SUJET_DÉMO_A1TP, front grid
DELF A2 tout public, official candidate paper SUJET_DÉMO_A2TP_02, front grid
Évolution des examens DELF/DALF — the 2024 reform
DELF B1 tout public, official candidate paper Sujet_démo_B1TP, front grid
DELF B2 tout public, official candidate paper SUJET_DÉMO_B2TP_02, front grid
A second official A2 paper, read specifically to re-check the exercise count
sources.note: Also 4 exercises in compréhension des écrits and also 1 h 40 collective. It carries no year and no reform marking, so it corroborates the 2019 paper and settles nothing about the current format.

caveat.en: Durations and marks are read from official candidate papers, all of which predate the 2024 reform. The reform replaced open answers with multiple choice in comprehension at A2–B2 and added ten minutes to the B1 written session, which is reflected above. THE NUMBER OF EXERCISES PER SECTION IS NOT VERIFIED FOR THE CURRENT FORMAT at any level: the reform states that comprehension now has more and shorter questions, and no post-2024 paper was obtainable. Two separate official A2 papers both show 4 exercises, and TWO PAPERS AGREEING ON A NUMBER THAT MAY BE OBSOLETE IS MORE MISLEADING THAN ONE. Corroboration between two sources of the same vintage is not independent evidence: both predate the reform, so they agree about the old format and say nothing about the current one.

structure.scope: C1 and C2, each read from an official candidate paper. C2 IS A DIFFERENT SHAPE from every other exam here — two papers marked out of 50 with a 10/50 minimum, not four out of 25 — which is why a guard written for DELF's shape must not be pointed at it.

sources.what: DALF C1, official candidate paper, épreuves collectives, front grid
DALF C2 Lettres et sciences humaines, official candidate paper Sujet_démo_C2
sources.note: Prints the candidate's choice of two domains — lettres et sciences humaines, or sciences — which the 2024 reform REMOVED. The paper therefore predates the reform, and that is how we know, rather than from a date on it.

sources.what: Évolution des examens DELF/DALF — the 2024 reform removed the DALF domain choice

caveat.en: Read from official candidate papers that predate the 2024 reform, which for DALF removed the choice of specialist domain. No change to DALF durations, marks or pass thresholds has been published that I could find, and no post-reform DALF paper was obtainable. Task counts are NOT VERIFIED for the current format.

passing.verified: printed on the front grid of each paper read

C1.minutesNote: environ. One long document of about eight minutes with two listenings, plus several short broadcast items with one. Documents 10 minutes maximum.

C1.task: one text of ideas, literary or journalistic, of 1,500 to 2,000 words
a synthesis from several documents totalling about 1,000 words, then an argued essay from their content
a presentation from several written documents, then a discussion with the panel

C2.minutesNote: passation 30 minutes; preparation 1 hour, after the two listenings
C2.task: report on a recorded document, personal development of its problem, then a debate with the panel
C2.domainChoice: The paper read offers lettres et sciences humaines or sciences. The 2024 reform removed this choice.

C2.task: produce a structured text — article, editorial, report, speech — from a dossier of about 2,000 words

structure.collectiveTotalNote: C1 4 hours, C2 3 h 30, both printed on the papers read. At C2 the oral is the individual paper, so the collective total and the written paper are the same 3 h 30.

compulsoryTotal.check: 25 + 15 + 45 = 85, which is the 1 h 25 the exam body states

scoring.note: Comprehension sections are scored on the 699 scale and weighted by question difficulty, not by a count of correct answers. The expression papers are marked out of 20.
scoring.verified: partial — the scale and bands are corroborated by several sources; the weighting statement is from a preparation site, not the exam body

forms.note: The candidate does not choose the form — the centre does — so a candidate must be ready for either, and the computer form is the faster of the two.

computer.note: Five extra items per skill, which do not count toward the score. The durations are unchanged, so the same 85 minutes covers 91 items instead of 76.

pace.why: The faster of the two, because the centre decides the form and a candidate trained to the slower pace would be unprepared for the other. Training to the harder case is safe; the reverse is not.

validity.portalClaims: NONE. The portal says nothing anywhere about validity, retakes or intervals — checked on 2026-10-04 across content/exams.json, the interface strings and every route. These figures are recorded so that the first such claim can be checked against them rather than written from memory.

structureUnverifiedWhileOffering.why: An unverified grid is honest; an unmarked claim is not. A learner who sees TEF listed must be able to see that this project has never checked what the TEF consists of.

structureNote: Every figure in an exam's `structure` block was read from the source named beside it on the date given. Nothing here is inferred from another figure, and nothing is carried over from an earlier version of this file: before 2026-10-04 this file carried no structure at all and `checkedOn` was null, while content/exam-papers.json stated an official duration that had never been checked — and one of them was wrong.
scopeNote: The portal's stated scope is every recognised French proficiency test: DELF, DALF, TCF and its variants, TEF and its variants. That is the owner's decision and it does not mean all of them are built — it means none is quietly absent and each carries either a verified structure or an explicit NOT VERIFIED with a reason. KNOWN GAP: the TEF variants (TEF Canada, TEFAQ, TEF Naturalisation, TEF IRN) are not enumerated here. They exist and are administered by the Chambre de commerce et d'industrie de Paris Île-de-France, but the agent has not verified the list of them, and inventing entries would be the same fault as inventing figures.
